title: Quantum Algorithms for Minimum Generating Set
authors: Bireswar Das, Udit Kumar, Kavita Samant, Dhara Thakkar
abstract: In this paper, we present a polynomial-time quantum algorithm for computing a minimum-sized generating set of solvable black-box groups. Next, we consider the class $Γ_d$ of black-box groups, where every non-abelian composition factor is isomorphic to a subgroup of the symmetric group $S_d$ for a fixed $d$. We design polynomial-time quantum algorithms to compute the direct product decomposition of abelian factor groups and solve the constructive membership problem for factor groups of groups from $Γ_d$. With the help of these algorithms, we design a quantum algorithm for computing a chief series of black-box groups from $Γ_d$. Using the chief series, we construct a polynomial-time quantum algorithm for computing minimum generating sets of black-box groups from $Γ_d$. Finally, we show that the minimum generating set problem for general black-box groups is in $\textrm{NP} \cap \textrm{coAM}$.
summary: This paper develops quantum algorithms to solve the minimum generating set problem for specific classes of black-box groups, particularly solvable groups and those in class $\Gamma_d$. It achieves this by recursively decomposing the group using its chief series and applying quantum techniques to factor quotient groups. The work establishes that the problem is solvable in polynomial time quantumly, advancing the theoretical understanding of quantum computation in group theory.
main_problem: The paper addresses the computational problem of finding the minimum size of a generating set (MIN-GEN) for a given black-box group.
main_result: It presents polynomial-time quantum algorithms for computing minimum generating sets for solvable black-box groups and for groups in the class $\Gamma_d$.
method: The approach involves designing recursive quantum algorithms that leverage the chief series decomposition of the group and utilize quantum oracles for group operations.
model_or_system: The work is situated in the black-box group model, where group operations are implemented via quantum oracles ($U_G, U_{G^{-1}}$) acting on qubits.
key_observables: The minimum number of generators, $d(G)$, and the structure of the chief series of the group.
important_parameters: The encoding length $n$ of the group elements, and the complexity bounds related to $\log |G|$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a chief series and relies on the black-box group model framework, which allows for polynomial-time quantum computation of various group-theoretic invariants.

paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing quantum algorithms for basic group properties (like composition series) to developing a recursive MIN-GEN algorithm based on the chief series decomposition, culminating in complexity proofs showing the problem is in AM.
why_interesting: While focused on abstract group theory, the development of polynomial-time quantum algorithms for complex structural problems like MIN-GEN demonstrates the power of quantum computation in solving classically hard computational problems.
